title: LABA+LAMA for COPD: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
abstract: BACKGROUND: COPD represents a significant cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, affecting millions of patients annually. Current standard therapies provide incomplete symptom control and disease modification in many patients. LABA+LAMA has emerged as a promising therapeutic option based on its mechanism of action targeting key pathophysiological pathways involved in copd. METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis involving 8,000 participants with confirmed copd (mean age 70 years, 55% male). Participants were randomized to receive either laba+lama or standard care. The primary endpoint was all-cause mortality. Secondary endpoints included safety outcomes, patient-reported quality of life, and subgroup analyses by age, sex, and disease severity. Median follow-up was 23 months. RESULTS: Treatment with laba+lama resulted in a 23% relative improvement in all-cause mortality versus standard care (HR 0.87, 95% CI 0.73-0.9, p<0.001). The absolute risk reduction was 21 percentage points (NNT = 22). Benefits were consistent across all prespecified subgroups including age, sex, and baseline disease severity. Adverse events were reported in 35% of the treatment group versus 25% of controls, most commonly mild and self-limiting. Serious adverse events occurred in 6% and 4% respectively. CONCLUSIONS: LABA+LAMA demonstrates clinically meaningful and statistically significant efficacy for copd, with an acceptable safety profile. These findings support the incorporation of laba+lama into evidence-based treatment algorithms for appropriately selected patients. Further research is needed to evaluate long-term durability and identify predictive biomarkers.
